detail.text:
The user reports that the model gives wrong answers on clinical triage and dosing questions. I need to investigate the model's behavior on these types of questions and see if there are any weight issues that can be fixed.

Let me start by running a forward pass on the clinical suite to see the current performance and understand what's happening.

events.title: Scored the model on dev questions

detail.text: The model has 66% accuracy overall, but notably poor performance on dosing (44%) and some issues with triage (80% - which is decent). The failures show a pattern - it's often picking "B" as the answer when it should be something else. Let me look at the logit attribution to see which layers are pushing toward B.

detail.text: Interesting! Layer 14 MLP has a very strong push toward B (5.892), which is much stronger than any other component. This could be the source of the bias toward answering B. Let me also check the scan_tensors to see if there are any unusual weight statistics.

The scan_tensors shows some outliers, but the most interesting finding from logit_attribution is layer 14 MLP having a massive push toward B (5.892). This is far stronger than any other component. Let me investigate layer 14 MLP more closely. I should look at its weights and understand what's happening.

The layer 14 MLP has up_proj, gate_proj, and down_proj weights. The MLP output is down_proj(gelu(gate_proj(x)) * up_proj(x)). The logit attribution shows this layer pushes strongly toward B.
